events.summary: Invisible, Lirael finds Turckle and Churckle overrun by Dragons Claw mercenaries. Neebus is running it badly, and the women from the Fark's Bargain brothel have set up shop there.
events.detail: Lirael gets hit by the door on the way in but stays undetected. Neebus is doing an expectedly terrible job of running the bar. The Fark's Bargain workers have moved in, though none of them appear to be demons. Milton is not there either. Zenya Kel is asleep at a table, drunk. Lirael uses suggestion to wake her and send her to the Moonwatch.

events.title: Brokk's Last Two Diamonds
events.summary: Brokk has only two diamonds left and pleads to keep one. Lirael's badge lets him buy both, and he does.
events.detail: Lirael goes to Brokk after failing to find Milton anywhere. Diamonds are what the party needs to bring back the dead. Brokk begs to hold one back, but the Sentinel badge settles it. On the walk back, Lirael finds Zenya passed out in the field next to the ship and carries her inside. By now everyone aboard is awake. Jazz is covered in rat hair from the bed Filgar used to sleep in.

events.title: The Great Repair Race
events.summary: Brand and Screech bet 100gp on who can finish repairing their side of the Moonwatch first. Brand wins, with some unrequested help from his nephew Brokk.
events.detail: The crew splits into two teams: Screech, Gorilla Beezel and Jeff against Brand, Sorenson and Jazz. Each team works one side of the ship, from the aft to the bow. Screech is pulling ahead when Brokk and Barry arrive at 10:30 to collect Sorenson, as promised. Brand says Sorenson is busy and Brokk can have him when the work is done. Brokk decides to pitch in, partly to speed things up and partly to show his uncle how it is really done. Brand finishes first, to Screech's surprise.

events.title: Eloria Arrives in Ardev
events.summary: A nervous Sazed meets Eloria off the military transport. She is elated that everyone is more or less okay and gives him a hug.
events.detail: Lirael told Felicia Jr to help Sazed prepare, but she has no idea what to do. Eloria only received the information the party gave Paxon after Lirael had been taken. Sazed introduces her to Felicia Jr, and the three go inside to decide what to do about Felicia Sr. Lirael's mother is still possessed and tied to her bed. They agree to search the Starilaskur Military Library for books on trance states before risking another battle with the Dreamweaver.

events.title: Dell Quickfoot's Warning
events.summary: The tortle reporter Dell Quickfoot arrives with two wereshark bodyguards. He tells Lirael there is no record of his crimes anywhere, and the Ardev Watch's reporting is a fraud.
events.detail: It is 11am; repairs are done and Brand lets Sorenson leave to record with Barry. Dell's bodyguards are the weresharks Topek and Wylon. When Dell raised the story with Helena, she forbade him from pursuing it, so he asked his friend Grib Grimley to look into it. Grib had been watching the Dragons Claw and Helena for some time. She told Dell she had something to share, and then she went missing. Dell fears this has grown far beyond protecting the paper's reputation. Lirael agrees to meet him at the Moonwatch at 9pm on the 23rd, and Dell lays low by crawling into his shell and having the weresharks carry him away.

events.title: Skye Lets Go
events.summary: Terrified of flying, Skye clings to Sazed's arm on the Moonwatch's flight deck. His stories give her the courage to let go and stand on her own.
events.detail: The party sweeps the ship and takes off at 1pm. Eloria gives the shifter children a check-up: they are emotionally battered but physically fine, and Skye refuses to be examined. Sazed tells Skye he is a loreguard working with the Sentinels, and that he found her village through a message from Carrk. On deck, Eloria wrangles the children and Screech lets one of them try flying, while Lirael casts calm emotions on Skye. Sazed tells her about hanging off the side of the ship and about prison, and she lets go of his arm. When she asks if she can stay with him, he says yes, but only if she becomes his loreguard apprentice; she needs to think about it.

events.title: A Lie for Listening Ears
events.summary: Lirael makes sure his possessed mother hears him say the party is heading to a secret base in White Horn Wood.
events.detail: Felicia Sr is still possessed, and anything she hears may reach the Dreamweaver. Lirael goes to her room and speaks the false destination clearly enough for her to catch it. Meanwhile the others have worked out how to stretch one diamond into two revivals with the ring of spell storing and a twinned spell. Eloria and Sazed put Jyo back together as best they can. The dead Flock changeling goes into the bag of holding for later.

events.title: Xera and Fey-Lynn Return
events.summary: Eloria stores Raise Dead in the ring of spell storing and Lirael twins it. On a single diamond, Xera and Fey-Lynn come back to life.
events.detail: Both women wake completely panicked. Lirael casts calm emotions on them. Xera finds her bearings fairly quickly and works out what happened and where she is. Fey-Lynn does not know who she is or where she is. Her mind feels empty and lonely. She asks to be left alone for a while.

events.title: Zenya Takes a Hostage, Briefly
events.summary: Zenya Kel wakes up aboard and tries to take Brand hostage while he plants a noise device in Felicia Sr's room. He disarms her in moments.
events.detail: Brand is installing the device so the party can talk without Felicia Sr overhearing. He easily disarms and restrains Zenya. She calms down as soon as she sees her sister and Felicia Jr. Then she starts flirting with everybody and talking without pause, which annoys everyone. She offers interior decorating advice, so Lirael takes her below deck to some art supplies. When the children come down, she starts doing arts and crafts with them.

events.title: Punch Me
events.summary: Lirael asks to be punched. Felicia's punch does nothing; Brand rolls a natural 20 for 13 damage.
events.detail: To get away from Zenya's chatter, Sazed and Eloria slip off to make tea for everyone. Sazed shows her the changes he has made to the recipe. Meanwhile Lirael asks someone to hit him. Felicia obliges with no effect at all. Brand does not hold back. Eloria and Sazed come back and serve the tea.

events.title: The Raven's Call
events.summary: An illusion guards Hearthsfire and teleports anyone who walks into it back out. Only a raven's call lets the party through.
events.detail: They land in a field near Hearthsfire in the Bears Wood and follow Carrk's coordinates on foot. Brand senses nature magic, but unlike a druid's it comes straight from the source. A raven looks at Sazed, caws, and passes through the illusion; when the party follows, they are bounced back out. Lirael imitates the call with minor illusion and passes through. Brand makes a terrible imitation of the caw and it works for him too. Sazed then makes the raven call he used to make and gets an answer. He remembers this magic: it is the kind of thing Spring Sagewood would do.

events.title: Hearthsfire Behind the Illusion
events.summary: Inside the hidden shifter village, Elder Falken Sagewood is overjoyed to see Sazed. He always believed Sazed had survived.
events.detail: Two guards, Fang and Brook, are shocked that outsiders found the place. Lirael explains he has a shifter friend just as Brand and Sazed come through the illusion. When Sazed says he has orphans from Stones Throw, the guards let them in despite their worries about outsiders. The villagers stare with suspicion as Fang leads them to Falken, the Elder of Vult. Falken is in conversation with Talon Bryn "The Bear" Wildheart of the Covenant of Emberfall, who is pleased to meet a mighty warrior. Falken rules that the outsiders may stay as long as they are with Sazed.

events.title: Should Carrk Keep the Ring?
events.summary: Falken tells Sazed privately that the elders are debating whether to strip Carrk Moonrunner of his place as the Ring of Siberys for failing to protect Stones Throw.
events.detail: Falken is glad of the orphans but surprised, because Carrk said there were no survivors. The Bear argues Carrk should be removed and says he has been acting strangely. Falken agrees in part but thinks Carrk may deserve another chance. Sazed vouches for Carrk and asks why the Bear was not at Stones Throw. The Bear answers that Glade Amberwood, the clan leader of Stones Throw, threw the Covenant out over a disagreement. Falken tells Sazed to go and speak with Carrk. Sazed was already no fan of the Covenant, and this bothers him.

events.title: Carrk at the Moon Stones
events.summary: Over Sylvan wine, Carrk Moonrunner says his fox totem lured him away from Stones Throw, and it was a Covenant druid in disguise. Before Sazed leaves, Carrk gives him a cloak.
events.detail: Carrk is praying at the Moon Stones when Sazed sits beside him, and he greets his old friend with an affectionate curse. He had feared Sazed was dead, but Falken told him to keep faith. Unusually outgoing for a shifter, he insists on wine first, served in the village's communal kitchen where everything is shared. His totem Foxtail appeared to warn him and led him away, and only too late did he learn it was a Covenant member in disguise. He killed the impostor and ran back, but the village was already gone, and he is wracked with grief. He also warns that the Covenant plans to make an example of Ardev to the Brelish government. As a parting gift he gives Sazed what he calls a Cloak of Displacement, carried for years, so Sazed won't get caught this time.

events.title: The Children of Stones Throw Come Home
events.summary: The party brings the orphans into Hearthsfire. The children are thrilled to see Fang, and the villagers' suspicion turns to guarded optimism.
events.detail: On the way, Sazed asks Skye about Carrk and the Covenant. She says the Covenant lived in the village until her father argued with them and threw them out. Carrk promised to protect them, but he was not there. Fang thanks Sazed; he left Stones Throw before the attack and never expected to see the children again. Falken is overjoyed and tells Sazed he has done it again. Sazed vouches for Carrk once more, and Falken agrees he should get another chance. Falken then sits down with Skye to talk about becoming a loreguard.

events.title: Spring and the Warding Tree
events.summary: At Garfan, the warding tree, Spring Sagewood compares Hearthsfire's uneasy pact with the Covenant to Sazed's with the Sentinels. She also senses that something has been attacking Brand's and Lirael's minds.
events.detail: Spring is in commune with the tree and knows they are there without looking up. Like everyone else she is delighted to see Sazed, whom she feared dead; it was she who answered his raven call. The illusion comes from Garfan itself, and Spring directs its magic. She complains that the young ones no longer take up the old magic. When Sazed presses her on the Covenant, she says Brelish society may seem welcoming but will not defend them when the moment comes. Glade learned that the hard way; shifters cannot survive in industrial society, and the Covenant understands that. Brand and Lirael deny anything is in their heads, but she insists they need not tell her what it is. She will consult Garfan on a way to protect their minds and asks them to come back.

events.title: Beware of Carrk
events.summary: Leaving for Ardev, the Bear stops Sazed outside Falken's home. Because he respects him as a warrior, he gives him a warning: beware of Carrk.
events.detail: The Bear admits they may disagree on much. He says his respect for Sazed is deep regardless. The warning comes without explanation. It is all the more pointed because Sazed has just vouched for Carrk twice. It also sits uneasily beside Carrk's own claim that the Covenant means to make an example of Ardev.

events.title: Why the Elders Fled Aundair
events.summary: Falken tells Sazed privately what became of the shifters after he was captured. The young grew reckless, Willow vanished, and the elders fled to Breland.
events.detail: The younger shifters began embezzling money directly from the Aundairian government. Willow warned them to stop before she disappeared; no one has seen her in eight years. With Willow gone and the danger growing, the elders left for Breland, where shifters are more accepted, and founded Hearthsfire. Falken has not seen his son in eight years. A year ago Glade broke away to found Stones Throw, believing closer ties to Brelish society were safe, despite Falken's warnings. Falken's last word is about changelings: never let them into the villages, for they bring only death and destruction. There are rumors Glade let changelings in before the massacre.

events.title: Skye Chooses Her Teacher
events.summary: After talking with Falken, Skye takes on the responsibility of becoming Sazed's loreguard initiate.
events.detail: On the flight deck Sazed had told her she could stay with him only as his apprentice, and she had asked for time to think. Falken's talk with her settles it. Sazed is now responsible for a student as well as his Sentinel duties. The other children stay in Hearthsfire, but Skye comes back aboard. The Moonwatch leaves for Starilaskur.

events.title: Shifters and the Industrial Age
events.summary: On the flight to Starilaskur, Sazed explains the shifter factions and the question that divides them: can shifters survive in a modern industrial society? Brand checks that he and Sazed are still cool.
events.detail: The flight is eight hours, but Brand spends two of them running the Moonwatch's boost, which can be used twice a day for an hour, and gets them there in six. Sazed lays out the different shifter factions and how they answer the industry question. Since industry is Brand's whole thing, he takes Sazed aside to make sure there is no bad blood. There isn't. Eloria fills the ring of spell storing with Raise Dead and Divination.

events.title: Questioning the Dead Changeling
events.summary: Eloria raises the dead Flock changeling. He names his village, Bravewind, which was attacked six weeks ago on the 11th of Vult.
events.detail: Asked about the day before his possession, he says his village was attacked; he ran, was kidnapped, and was put through a portal. While possessed, his instructions were to use disguise self to trick, steal and kill, to kidnap the drow, and to kill the dwarf and the shifter. He points to Bravewind's location on the map, near Ardev. The Flock's soldiers were stolen people, not volunteers.

events.title: Xera's Thank-You Kiss
events.summary: Xera asks Lirael to confirm that her memories of what happened are true, then kisses him for reviving her.
events.detail: Coming back from the dead has left her exhausted. Lirael lets her rest in his room. Felicia finds the kiss disgusting and leaves. Eloria thinks it is cute.

events.title: Paxon Traces the Lightning Rail
events.summary: Paxon calls with a lead: the lightning rail was switched on from the Starilaskur Military Railway Junction at midnight on the 21st.
events.detail: This is the rail line that carried the train the party fought aboard. Someone at the junction turned it on. Paxon says the party can go there and find out who did it. The lead gives them a second reason to be in Starilaskur besides the library.

events.title: Griffith and the Hippogriff
events.summary: Starilaskur's air traffic control is cool and professional. A halfling named Griffith, riding a hippogriff, guides the Moonwatch in.
events.detail: After Ardev, a competent landing is a novelty. Starilaskur is a mining and military town. Griffith will turn up again; Beezel later spends his guard shift joking around with him. The party heads straight for the Extra Planar Task Force.

events.title: Paladins at the Door
events.summary: Captain Opal Dane-Oriel of the Extra Planar Task Force answers the door. At the sound of Lirael's name, her paladins prepare to fight.
events.detail: The party flashes their badge, and the EPTF has already worked out what the Sentinels are. Lirael's name changes everything: the task force remembers the massacre a year ago. Lirael's detect thoughts shows him Dane's memory of the ritual's aftermath, the Watchers of the Gate all turned to gore, and she is furious. Lirael tells her the Dreamweaver had possessed him and that he is now free. Dane casts detect magic to check whether that is true.

events.title: The Truth Amulet at the EPTF
events.summary: Dane recognises the Amulet of Compulsive Truth. Wearing it, Lirael proves he was possessed and Brand proves he was framed, and she orders her troops to stand down.
events.detail: Lirael produces the amulet and Dane knows it for what it is. Under its compulsion he repeats that the Dreamweaver possessed him. Brand asks whether the Broadhelm name carries more weight here. Dane says it does, until she learns he is Brand, the man who tried to kill the king. Brand puts on the amulet and proves he was framed. It is a lot for Dane to take in, but she tells her paladins to stand down.

events.title: The Task Force's Blind Spot
events.summary: The EPTF never took the Dreamweaver seriously. Lirael Sr's ravings and the Watchers' massacre had turned them off it, and now Dane has no choice.
events.detail: Lirael's father had once come to the task force, and his apparent insanity discredited the whole subject. The massacre by the Watchers of the Gate made it worse. Dane reveals she has just captured Watchers trying to restart the cult in the Witches Waltz. The EPTF used to ignore the cult but has cracked down since the massacre. Halfway through that fight, the warlocks lost their powers. Brand notices a portrait of a warforged named Bulwark Broadhelm on the wall but says nothing.

events.title: Elfina Daelmourn
events.summary: The captured Grand Witch learns that Lirael killed her father. Hearing he was dreamwoven, she panics, until they convince her he is free.
events.detail: Elfina is the daughter of Grand Warlock Maldroc Daelmourn, the former head of the cult. Maldroc met with Lirael Sr and performed the ritual with Lirael. Lirael admits he killed her father, but says he was dreamwoven at the time. She did not know anyone could become undreamwoven, and it takes time to calm her. Once convinced, she scolds Dane for not taking the party seriously. After her father's death she wanted to follow in his footsteps and restart the Watchers. The cult's literature was burned after the massacre, but she had kept some at her house.

events.title: Who the Watchers Were
events.summary: Elfina explains that the Watchers of the Gate were celestial warlocks devoted to The Fury. They guarded the Gate until a worthy bearer of the Obelisk came along.
events.detail: She knows about the knowledge curse and about the Skull Knight. During the fight with the EPTF she heard The Fury call out for help. Then it cried out in anguish. After that her powers stopped working, and she has not heard from her patron since. Without the Gate, without the literature and without their powers, she believes the Watchers are finished.

events.title: A Reason to Wait
events.summary: Lirael reads Elfina's thoughts. Now that someone is finally taking her seriously, she has decided to put off ending her life.
events.detail: Lirael promises her they will come back. On the way out, Brand asks Dane what the Broadhelm forge means to Starilaskur. To a mining and military town, Dane says, it is everything. Ember runs it. That answer sends Brand toward a reunion forty years overdue.

events.title: The Warforged Named Broadhelm
events.summary: Dane tells them about Bulwark Broadhelm, a good EPTF soldier who saved many men. He left the task force and died aboard the Kason in Karrnath two weeks ago.
events.detail: Brand had seen the warforged's portrait and kept quiet about it. Now he learns a Broadhelm creation served and died a hero. Dane does not trust the party enough to leave them alone. They say they will step outside to talk and be right back. They leave instead.

events.title: Arkhan's Library
events.summary: At the Military Library, Arkhan, a librarian even more awkward than Sazed, helps them find books on trance states. Sazed learns a crude version of the Bloodmoon Ritual.
events.detail: Arkhan has an encyclopedic knowledge of books, and of trains. Lirael summons Jeff for help. Lirael also asks Arkhan where he gets his style, and the answer is Wendel's Wares. Brand checks out books on the history of technology and the lightning rail, and learns the layout of the current and former train stations. Sazed tells Skye she must choose a field of study as a loreguard. She picks combat and the history of war, so he takes out war histories for her and medical texts for himself.

events.title: Gelard Greenly's Overdue Books
events.summary: Arkhan reveals the trance-state books were recently borrowed by Gelard Greenly, a young, eccentric and slightly crazed wizard who has been checking out everything on the Dreamweaver and possession.
events.detail: The books are popular and due back in two days, and Arkhan complains that Gelard never returns anything. Lirael uses his badge to see the recent records, which show Gelard's reading list. Older records are kept deep in the salt mine. Lirael checks out every book Gelard has returned, about three quarters of them, plus some sorcerer texts. Everything is due in two weeks except the trance books. The party has no intention of returning those, hoping to draw Gelard out.

events.title: Salutes on Recruitment Row
events.summary: Brand warns a young dwarf against enlisting. The boy answers that he will be drafted anyway, so he might as well join now.
events.detail: Walking through Starilaskur's lively nightlife, the party passes young men signing up for the military. Lirael disagrees with Brand; he understands wanting control over your own destiny. The dwarf thanks Brand, then asks Skye's name and calls her cute. The party leaves promptly, but not before saluting the recruits and getting salutes back. Further down the street they watch a draft dodger being arrested.

events.title: Ember Broadhelm
events.summary: At the Broadhelm forge, Brand's twin sister greets him coldly. He returns the coldness, and then they embrace.
events.detail: Ember introduces herself to the party. She asks whether Brand liked the packages she sent him in prison; he never received any. She has a daughter now, Ash, who works at the forge in Sharn. Ember offers the good news or the bad news first. They ask for the bad, and she pours everyone dwarven ale.

events.title: The Broadhelm Family Falls Apart
events.summary: Ember explains that after Brand's imprisonment their father grew paranoid. He sealed away the forge's inventions, refused to pass it on, and the family scattered.
events.detail: Their father took full control of the forge and refuses to release anything, fearing what happened to Brand. Mason and Cutter cope by building stranger and stranger things that will never see daylight. They built the warforged Bulwark for no reason and never raised him. Forge turned to the Church to preach the word of Onatar, and Ember came to Starilaskur to build arms for the front. Art left to join House Cannith, where he is the only one whose inventions get released, and Cannith now outpaces the Broadhelms. Ember is the only one still talking to everyone; their father and Art have not spoken in years. She believes Brand may be the only one who can fix it, and he needs to go to Sharn and talk to their father. Thaddeus has never stopped trying to get the suit's blueprints, and the Broadhelms spit at his name.

events.title: The Ring of Cure Racism
events.summary: Ember warns Brand he won't like who Ash's father is: an elf. The party teases him, and Ember produces a Ring of Cure Racism.
events.detail: Ember says the relationship is complicated, another reason she left for Starilaskur. Brand is visibly upset, which only encourages the teasing. The ring is Ember's answer. Lirael makes a crude comment and is nearly hit by both Broadhelms' Thunder Gauntlets at once.

events.title: Ember's Forty-Year Suit
events.summary: For the good news, Ember opens a wall to reveal the suit of armor she has been building for Brand for forty years. It has never worked until Brand seats Onatar's holy core inside it.
events.detail: Ember has never been able to get the suit running. Brand shows the party the holy core that powers his old suit. He does not quite know how he did it, but the core came from Onatar, and it is what Thaddeus wants. He installs it, the new suit comes to life, and he climbs in. He gives his old suit to his sister. The twins have a little manly cry.

events.title: Joke Potions and a Goblin Brand
events.summary: Ember hands over the joke items the Soul Street Hooligan keeps trying to steal: a Potion of Become Rock and a Potion of Attacked by Birds. Brand tries the ring and becomes a goblin.
events.detail: Skye has started stumbling; she is getting slightly drunk. She has never drunk before, because her father Glade was a teetotaller, though when Sazed knew him he was a drunk. Asked for more items, Ember reveals that Gelard has asked for strange items to relieve a possession. He won't say what kind, which makes them impossible to make. She also gives the party three greater healing potions. Brand now owes his sister two favours. Then he uses the Ring of Cure Racism to turn himself into a goblin, which is funny.

events.title: Race to the Moonwatch
events.summary: Outside the forge, the party spots Killian, Kynds, Darvok and EEEEE the Dwarf in a Can loading new weapons and armor onto a carriage. Both sides race for the Moonwatch.
events.detail: The carriage barrels over the tables in a square and swerves into a nearby alley. Sazed sprints ahead to cut it off. Lirael casts Hypnotic Pattern, filling the alley with an illusion of dancing dwarves in their underthings. Every Aundairian except Killian is charmed.

events.title: Mine Cart, Crane, Roof, Living Room
events.summary: Brand tries to jump a gap, the rocks give way, and he lands in a mine cart. He blasts it toward a crane, swings onto a roof, and falls through into a couple's home.
events.detail: He propels the cart with his Thunder Gauntlets. The crane carries him onto a roof that cannot hold him. The couple inside panic. Sazed, seeing no carriage arrive, runs back and finds the Aundairians charmed in the alley. Brand eventually runs out of the house, chased by the couple and a police officer. He flashes his badge and keeps running to help Sazed.

events.title: The Rod, Elwood and the Axe
events.summary: Lirael's mage hand sticks the immovable rod to the carriage. Jeff recognises EEEEE as "Elwood", Sazed kills him, and Killian's new battle axe takes half of Sazed's health in one cleave.
events.detail: Lirael places the rod on the back of the carriage so it cannot move. Killian shakes EEEEE out of the spell and tries to drive off, but the carriage is stuck. Jeff arrives, and Lirael tells him to help. Jeff knows the Dwarf in a Can by his real name, Elwood. Sazed kills EEEEE quickly and squares off against Killian. Lirael moves the rod to the front of the cart and starts throwing fire bolts at Killian.

events.title: Jeff Swallows the Aundairians
events.summary: Jeff swallows Kynds and is told to spit him out. He swallows Killian and is told the same. Outnumbered and disarmed, Killian surrenders.
events.detail: Sazed is the one who tells Jeff to spit Kynds out, and the halfling uses the moment to flee down the alley. Jeff then swallows Killian and gets the same request. Sazed takes Killian's new battle axe. With his crew charmed, dead or gone and no weapon in hand, Killian gives up. The session was later titled "Which Guy Do You Want Me To Swallow."

events.title: Kynds Slips Away
events.summary: Sazed chases Kynds across the rooftops of Starilaskur, but the halfling is gone.
events.detail: Brand and Lirael stay behind to explain the chaos to the approaching police. Sazed climbs onto the houses to look for Kynds. He tells a police officer he is on Sentinel business and asks if a halfling ran by. The officer points the way, but Sazed cannot find him. He returns to the party empty-handed.

events.title: Darvok Shouts for Aundair
events.summary: Killian denies being Aundairian, until a freshly uncharmed Darvok shouts his allegiance to Aundair in front of Sergeant Taggart.
events.detail: Taggart of the Starilaskur Military Police arrives expecting an explanation, and the party's badges satisfy him. Darvok, just out of the charm and unaware of his surroundings, gives the game away. The police take Darvok, but the party keeps Killian for questioning. Jeff says Elwood was a jerk and he wishes he had killed him himself. He spits on the body, and the party lets him go. The Dwarf in a Can is back in the party's hands.

events.title: King Boranel's Little Secret
events.summary: Killian taunts the officers that they cannot even ask who gives their orders, then names the party as Sentinels. Brand knocks him out.
events.detail: The officer Sazed spoke to on the rooftops asks Taggart what a Sentinel is. Taggart reprimands him for asking questions after a badge has been shown. Killian seizes on it and tells everyone the party are Sentinels. King Boranel's little secret can't be kept from the public forever, he says, and asks what will happen then. Brand knocks him unconscious to shut him up. He then takes the Aundairians' armor and weapons back to his sister.

events.title: This Is Not Your Refuge
events.summary: Lirael uses Divination to ask whether bringing Elfina aboard is wise. He is engulfed in blinding light and sees a red dragon.
events.detail: Sazed and Lirael drive the Aundairians' carriage back toward the Moonwatch, watching for Kynds all the way, and hand it to a military police officer. Beezel is joking around with Griffith, unbothered; he thought they were never in real trouble. Sazed orders him back to his post. The vision speaks: "This is not your refuge, seeker... but you are welcome in it." And: "Your mistrust is misplaced." Aboard, Eloria has built a makeshift chapel to Dol Arrah out of random items. Skye is electric with excitement and brags about how fast she ran back, and Sazed is just glad she is all right.

events.title: Broadhelms Come in All Shapes
events.summary: Still a goblin, Brand returns to the house he crashed through and claims to be a Broadhelm. The couple don't believe him until he fixes their roof for free.
events.detail: They reluctantly lend him a ladder. He climbs up and uses mending on the hole, but gets the ladder stuck inside. He breaks the ladder and mends it again to free it. The husband concludes that "maybe Broadhelms come in all shapes and sizes," which stirs something in Brand's stubborn dwarven heart. Back on the ship, he hears about Beezel's disappointing performance. The party vents to Eloria about the quality of their crew. There is a reason they got their own ship so soon: they are the outcast misfits of the Sentinels.

events.title: We Don't Die
events.summary: Below deck, Zenya has used Chester as an art caddy to make a garish pink banner. It carries a rhinestone seal of Breland and the slogan "We Don't Die".
events.detail: It is well made but gaudy, and the party decides to encourage her. Erald reveals that Dandy is going crazy building a tea machine to outdo Sazed and Eloria. Sazed gives Skye the books he picked out for her; she is thrilled, and has had a great day. They tie Killian up in a storage room. Skye asks to stand guard and Sazed allows it, with Eloria guarding too to coach her. The two have an awkward but cute moment parenting Skye together, and Eloria gets embarrassed praising Sazed's abilities.

events.title: Too Powerful for Patrol
events.summary: Felicia Jr is angry she wasn't taken on patrol when Skye was. Lirael explains it's the opposite: she is too powerful and has to learn control first.
events.detail: Lirael gives her Chicken Soup for the Sorcerer's Soul. She has been around longer than Skye and asks if she isn't good enough. When she asks to spar Skye, Lirael says not now, because he worries she might kill her. That strokes her ego nicely and she calms down to study her new books. She shows off prestidigitation again, saying she doesn't know what it's called, and Lirael admits he doesn't either. She is worried about feeding their mother, so Sazed and Eloria set up an IV for Felicia Sr.

events.title: Carrk's Cloak Connects to Another Plane
events.summary: As Sazed attunes to Carrk's gift, Brand feels dark magic coming off it. Identify reveals a cloak of connect mind, linked to a being on another plane, presumably the Dreamweaver.
events.detail: Brand begins attuning to Sazed's old Cloak of Displacement while Sazed reads his medical texts. Then Sazed starts attuning to the new cloak from Carrk. Once Brand finishes, he senses the dark energy and tells Sazed to stop, and he does. Identify shows the cloak is not what Carrk claimed. Brand gives the old cloak back to Sazed. Meanwhile Xera has been waiting for Lirael in his room, and everybody knows how they spent the time. Brand and Sazed fill Lirael in, and they decide to delay the return to Hearthsfire.

events.title: Stowaways in a Bag of Holding
events.summary: To get into the Starilaskur Military Railway Junction, Brand and Lirael hide in the bag of holding and breathe through a metal tube while an invisible Sazed carries them in.
events.detail: Before leaving, Brand changes into his stealth suit, gives Beezel another dad lecture, and confiscates his comic: Brelish Action Comics 146, The Escapades of Sergeant Blazehelm. At the junction Brand notices Lirael's bag is open. The Potion of Become Rock and the Potion of Attacked by Birds are gone, replaced by a note: "Thanks for the Magic Items - Soul Street Hooligan." Inside, they communicate through Lirael's telepathy. Sazed cannot pick the employees-only lock, so Lirael conjures a minor illusion of a trash can to cover Sazed opening the bag, and Brand picks it. They head down to the rail, stepping around a trip wire.

events.title: Orange Fur on the Cleared Track
events.summary: In the old unfinished station below the junction, one track has been freshly cleared. Sazed finds soldiers' bootprints and tufts of orange fur.
events.detail: The station is in bad shape, full of rubble, with one track broken. Brand traces the pipes feeding elemental energy to the rail up into the ceiling and to an office in the corner. Sazed runs up the wall and kicks at the door. It is opened by Chaton E'Clair, the station master, an orange tabaxi. Sazed flips into the room above him and makes a small noise; Chaton rolls a 1, blames the wind, and goes back to his paperwork. Using Brand's knowledge of the lightning rail, Sazed works out that the wall of switches behind Chaton controls the railway. This is how the rail was turned on.

events.title: Chaton's Catnip
events.summary: A train conductor delivers the package Chaton has been waiting for. He thinks it is catnip, and it explodes when he opens it, killing him.
events.detail: The party is debating telepathically whether to question or kidnap Chaton when someone knocks on the outer door. Chaton signs quickly; the box smells off, but he ignores it. Sazed dodges the blast. Outside, two conductors on the carriage horses watch the explosion without expression, and Sazed leaps onto the carriage roof as it heads into town. Once out of sight, the conductors tear off their clothes to reveal Starilaskur Military Police uniforms and change their faces. They are changelings. The carriage pulls up at the Broadhelm forge.

events.title: A Package for Ember
events.summary: A changeling brings Ember a package "from Tobias Gildenforge." Lirael's warning arrives, Sazed cuffs the bomber, and Brand reaches his sister just in time to be blown up beside her.
events.detail: Lirael sends Ember a message warning her. Sazed jumps off the carriage, races inside and handcuffs the changeling, and he and Ember start beating him. The changeling opens the package anyway, and the blast catches Brand. The second changeling opens the back of the carriage and frees a gorgon. Its petrifying breath turns a police officer to stone as he tries to close the town gate. Lirael shuts the forge door and fights the changeling while the gorgon batters the door down. Ember and her artificers put out the fire.

events.title: Off the Cliff, Into the Gorgon
events.summary: The last changeling flees through the closing gate. Sazed leaps off a cliff to kill it with a flying unarmed strike, and then the party brings down the gorgon.
events.detail: Brand freezes the gate chains with Ray of Frost to slow them and give Sazed time to get through. The gorgon breaks through the door and tries to gore Lirael. Ember comes out of the forge and turns her flamethrower on it. Sazed returns from the kill. Out of breath and trapped in a small space where it cannot charge, the gorgon is overwhelmed. Ember gives Brand haste, and her flamethrower and his missile launcher finish it.

events.title: Sigils Up, Captain Dane Furious
events.summary: The explosions push the EPTF to raise the town's defensive sigils. Captain Dane arrives furious, and every time the explanation starts going well, Brand makes a jab.
events.detail: A defensive barrier rises over Starilaskur and a drunken crowd gathers as the police cordon off the scene. A drunk Jeff appears and is sent back to the Pickled Pegasus. Sergeant Taggart predicts the party's explanation but wants to hear it anyway. He believes every word and is ready to go full detective. Missing the Dreamweaver is a big mistake for the EPTF, and if Dane has nothing to show for it when Major Highfire returns, she will be in deep trouble. Taggart says he will talk to her. She will watch over the town while he investigates with the party.

events.title: Horses from First Tower
events.summary: Beezel interrogates the changelings' horses. With a map and some analysis, the party learns the bombers came from First Tower.
events.detail: Lirael reads Taggart's mind to be sure of him and finds nothing but detective thoughts. They load the dead changeling into its carriage and take it to the police station, while Lirael talks telepathically with Dane; she believes him about the Dreamweaver but is unsure about trusting the party. In Taggart's office, they explain as little as they can, and he is hooked by the mystery. The horses are stupid, but the travel time shows the changelings set out after the Dreamweaver threatened Ember and the Sagewoods, before the train battle. Taggart is relieved they hadn't been under his nose, and keeps the horses for later. At the closed railway they collect Chaton's body and find nothing else in his wrecked office. The party agrees: Taggart is cool.

events.title: The Hooligan's Saxophone Solo
events.summary: Sazed catches the Soul Street Hooligan sliding the Ring of Cure Racism off Brand's finger. The thief escapes behind a hypnotic saxophone solo.
events.detail: The party is watching their belongings carefully on the walk to the EPTF. When Sazed grabs his hand, the Hooligan protests that he is only taking his own items. They tell him that is stealing, and he says yes. They try to catch him for the bounty, but he casts a Hypnotic Pattern of himself playing a blazing saxophone solo, and everyone is entranced. He thanks them for the items and says he knows someone who really needs the ring. He gives each of them a free ticket to any Soul Street Hooligan show and runs off into the night.

events.title: Elfina Walks Free
events.summary: This time Brand just smiles and flatters Captain Dane, and she agrees Elfina is more trouble than she is worth. Elfina is thrilled to be free.
events.detail: The paladins are busy powering the defensive sigils. The party convinces Dane they are doing the EPTF a favour by taking Elfina off its hands. On the walk to the Witches Waltz, Elfina proves strange. She asks what they sacrificed for their powers and whether they hear demons when they cast. The Fury had the Watchers sacrifice animals and hold other strange rites. They explain that not all magic is gained by losing something and that she doesn't have to do any of that anymore. They give her pamphlets on the Sovereign Host, benevolent gods she could devote herself to.

events.title: Flashback in the Witches Waltz
events.summary: Lirael collapses on the threshold of the cult's hall. In a vision, the visitor asks if he wants to remember, and he finally sees the massacre.
events.detail: They enter with their badges, and Lirael immediately passes out. He sees the Watchers of the Gate and Elfina's father, Maldroc Daelmourn, begin the ritual. The mirrors become doorways into the astral sea. The Dreamweaver possesses Lirael. He kills the Watchers, tearing their bodies apart until nothing is left but gore. Then he burns the library.

events.title: Hiding in a Cart
events.summary: Slaps and water can't wake Lirael. When he comes to, he runs, and Brand and Sazed find him hiding in a cart, crying.
events.detail: Brand and Sazed carried him outside the moment he fell. Nothing they try brings him round, and he wakes from the vision on his own. They calm him down, and he tells them what he saw. The party goes back into the Witches Waltz and destroys every mirror. They take what little remains of the library. Elfina pulls her father's writings from beneath the floorboards.

events.title: Kynds Takes Killian Back
events.summary: Back at the Moonwatch, Kynds stands on deck with a crew of Aundairian hobgoblins, a charmed Beezel and crossbows aimed. He doesn't want a fight; he just wants his captain.
events.detail: Sazed notices something is off as they arrive. They agree and send Lirael inside for Killian. Sazed tries to talk, saying he is Kynds's friend, and Kynds answers that if that's true he'll hand Killian over, but it is too tense to reach an understanding. Inside, Eloria is looking after an upset Skye, who is coming down from being a little drunk. Screech's conversation with Fey-Lynn seems to have calmed her. Lirael has Eloria bring Killian up and has Screech ready a possible ambush. Kynds is too alert for Lirael to sneak up on, so they give him his captain and the Aundairians slowly leave.

events.title: Eloria's Ashhaven
events.summary: Sazed kicks a crate on the lower deck, torn between Sentinel duty, old loyalties and Skye. Eloria follows and tells him her village, Ashhaven, was wiped out in an early Aundairian invasion.
events.detail: Beezel is upset about being charmed, and Brand gives him a pep talk. Sazed goes below and takes his anger out on a crate. Eloria tells him about Ashhaven, destroyed at the very start of the war; it is what she had been sharing with Skye earlier. She makes him feel better about his situation and his competence. They realise they are more alike than they thought and share a cute little cuddle.

events.title: A Room for Elfina, a Kiss for Sazed
events.summary: The Moonwatch leaves Starilaskur for Ardev. Lirael shows Elfina a room of her own, and Eloria kisses Sazed on the cheek and runs off.
events.detail: Elfina is thrilled with the room. Lirael tells her this is as good as it gets. Sazed and Eloria cuddle before bed. She gives him a kiss on the cheek and runs away before he can react.

events.title: The Emotional Damage Sempenator
events.summary: Brand helps Dandy finish his tea machine. He replaces its hand crank with a combustion engine powered by Dandy's Fire Bolt.
events.detail: It takes some convincing before Dandy accepts help. His Emotional Damage Sempenator only reaches the halfway mark on the crank. Brand's engine pushes it to full emotional damage. They taste the tea, and both of them hear squirrels insulting them.

events.title: A Nightmare in Song
events.summary: Brand has a nightmare, for once not the Dreamweaver's doing, of Sorenson singing "Thaddeus is coming to town."
events.detail: Thaddeus D'Cannith is an elf and the Head Baron of House Cannith, rival to the Broadhelm Forge and heir to the house. He and Brand were once friendly rivals. When Brand refused to give him the plans to his suit, Thaddeus framed him for attempting to kill King Boranel. Brand spent forty years in prison for it. The dream turns out to be a warning of sorts.

events.title: Lirael's Morning Rounds
events.summary: Up first, Lirael warns Elfina to remember the knowledge curse. Then his sister insists on a handshake and hits him with Shocking Grasp.
events.detail: He tells Elfina to keep what she knows about the Dreamweaver close to her chest. She asks whether she should remove the runes she painted on herself, and he says no. Felicia has been reading the sorcery books he bought her. Lirael is glad she is learning but tells her not to test spells on him. He spends the rest of the time before the others wake patrolling the ship.

events.title: Felicia Confronts Elfina
events.summary: A crash and screams bring Lirael below deck. Felicia is wreathed in fire, demanding to know why a woman covered in the Fury's runes is on the ship.
events.detail: Elfina is cowering in terror, and Lirael's calm emotions does not work on Felicia. He stands between them and explains Elfina has no powers anymore and is only here for information. Felicia turns invisible and Elfina flees to her room and locks the door. Faerie fire fails to find Felicia, but detect thoughts locates her in her room, wondering why the Fury chose her as its vessel and not Elfina. She is angry Lirael didn't tell her and calls him a jerk, but she listens. She accepts Elfina may be useful for information, but after that she wants her gone. Elfina refuses to leave her room and says she will wash off her makeup; Lirael was right, this is as good as it got.

events.title: Steve and Bob's Lost Sons
events.summary: A thud wakes the ship. The blue dragon Steve the Skycracker and his friend, the red dragon Bob the Blazebringer, have landed on the Moonwatch to demand a favour.
events.detail: Steve says the party has trespassed in his skies again and owes him their lives for not killing them the first time. He and Bob want the party to find their sons, Richard and Bill, last seen heading toward Ardev. The sons now call themselves Ragnarok of Eberron: Bringer of Untimely Doom, and Balthazar of the Wastes: The Last Face You'll Ever See. Both fathers are disgusted by the names. Fetching the boys is too lowly a task for dragons but would be a legendary quest for mortals, and Steve may grant free passage through his skies in return. Before leaving, Bob mentions a massive, gaudy ship they just passed, full of rude elves.

events.title: The Empyrean in Their Spot
events.summary: Arriving in Ardev, they find Thaddeus's ship, The Empyrean, in the Moonwatch's usual spot. It is as massive and gaudy as the dragons said.
events.detail: Brand can tell the ship is built with Broadhelm workmanship, specifically Art's. Sazed notices that Ardev's air traffic control is, for once, actually competent. Daedalus is watching the ship, along with some birds. The man who stole forty years of Brand's life has arrived in town.

events.title: Squirrels in the Tea
events.summary: At breakfast, Dandy serves tea from his finished machine. Everyone who drinks it hears squirrels insulting them.
events.detail: Sazed and Brand finish their long rest. Sazed checks on Skye, who is a little hungover; Zenya is doing her makeup, heavily. Zenya complains about the lack of mirrors, and Sazed insists there is a good reason for that. At the meal the crew points out Skye's makeup and she goes to wash it off. Dandy feels he has shown up Eloria and Sazed and proven what real culinary art is. Sazed suggests he stop worrying about artistic statements and just make food.

events.title: Brand Goes Purple
events.summary: With Thaddeus in town, the party decides Brand needs a disguise. Zenya paints him purple, and he puts on the hat of slight disguise.
events.detail: Thaddeus has never stopped trying to get his hands on Brand's suit, and the holy core that powers it. A Broadhelm walking around Ardev would be noticed. Zenya, with her art supplies, is happy to oblige. The result is purple, not subtle.

events.title: A Message for the Lighted One
events.summary: During Eloria's animal chapel, a female bird arrives and Mr. Beaks bows and offers her cheese. When Skye calls it cute, the bird turns to her and speaks.
events.detail: Eloria is holding chapel for Rufus and Mr. Beaks when the bird lands, and Mr. Beaks starts sharing his pile of cheese with her. The message to Skye: "You aren't alone, Lighted one. There is power in you. Return to your home, your family need not die in vain. Bring the Guarded One." Brand recognises the spell as Animal Messenger. Sazed knows the phrase Guarded One; it is what the Bloodsinger calls him. Lighted One must be Skye, so the Bloodsinger wants them both at Stones Throw. They decide to go after Thaddeus's speech.

events.title: Screech's Bedtime Stories
events.summary: Screech doesn't show up for breakfast. Expecting the worst, the party finds him comforting Fey-Lynn with the story of how they stole the Moonwatch.
events.detail: He has been telling her stories of the party's exploits since she was revived. He has been sleeping on the floor so she can have the bed. Fey-Lynn says she wants to visit Canuck. She seems more stable now. She is ready to talk about her possession.

events.title: Fey-Lynn's Debrief: Three Phases
events.summary: Fey-Lynn explains what the Dreamweaver used her for. She steered the magic society toward Karrnath, fed The Right Hand false data, and watched the Xal'ris.
events.detail: She was to convince the society that most Dreamweaver activity was in Karrnath and to take the opposite stance to Lirael Sr, discrediting his ideas. Adding The Right Hand to the society let the Dreamweaver feed him faulty data to share at meetings. When the party came to town, it warned her and ordered phase one: mislead them. It took note of everything they told her they had discovered about it, and was enraged to learn Lirael could read minds. Phase two was capturing Lirael's mother to set a trap to possess the party. Phase three was killing them outright. That is all she knows.

events.title: Who Burned Stones Throw?
events.summary: Skye asks Sazed who really wiped out her village. He tells her it was the Silver Flame, which confuses her: the Silver Flame in Ardev has only ever been kind to her family.
events.detail: They talk below deck after breakfast. She is friends with Wilford Chism. Every year on Reconciliation Day, the Ardev church threw a party for the shifters. The answer does not fit anything she knows.

events.title: Wilford's Mushroom Warning
events.summary: Sorenson returns to the ship with Wilford Chism close behind, clearly annoying him. Wilford ate a lot of mushrooms and got an ominous warning from his god.
events.detail: Wilford explains once again how mushrooms can bring you closer to god. He hears his god's messages more clearly than ever, and he knows the party is experiencing the same thing. His son Jazz is busy preparing for the speech, so he went to Sorenson for protection. He asks to stay on the Moonwatch for the time being, and the party agrees.

events.title: Reconciliation Day
events.summary: Wilford explains Reconciliation Day, a Silver Flame holiday of penance and giving back to the shifter community. Ardev's elderly, moderate church could never have attacked Stones Throw.
events.detail: Wilford has a small moment with Skye. He asks why he hasn't seen the shifters lately, and she tells him about the attack. He explains the holiday to Sazed. He is preparing funerals for Turckle and the Valviers and invites the party if they can make it.

events.title: Murderer Leaves Ardev
events.summary: Sorenson brings the latest Ardev Watch: "Murderer Leaves Ardev: Is Our Nightmare Finally Over?" It celebrates Lirael's departure and urges the town to revolt if he returns.
events.detail: The tone is tempered rejoicing, hoping he never returns but wary that he will. The paper backs the curfew and wants it continued indefinitely, claiming the recent attacks would never have happened under one. The party knows from overhearing The Right Hand and Gelford, and from reading The Right Hand's mind, that they intend to keep the curfew forever. The paper may be selling it to the public in advance. The second article heaps praise on Thaddeus as a master creator and orator and urges everyone to attend his speech. It even credits House Cannith for bringing free entertainment to Breland in a time of war.

events.title: Dinner on the Empyrean
events.summary: Sorenson describes recording with Barry and Gribble Goblin in the new Cannith Recording Studio below the forge. Afterwards Thaddeus took the musicians to dinner on The Empyrean.
events.detail: Thaddeus wears an anti-magic amulet. Brand remembers it from their friendship, when Thaddeus grew paranoid about magical technology and started wearing it. Art Broadhelm, who built the ship, was at the dinner, along with a very attractive tiefling butler named Silvania. Sorenson found Thaddeus weirdly charming but fake. He had the band play a set and asked them to play again before his speech. Sorenson is not sure that will still happen, because Barry Baritone has gone missing. Thaddeus offered the band beds aboard for the night, but Sorenson felt weird about it and left.

events.title: The Last of the Gorgis Family
events.summary: Leaving the Empyrean, Sorenson visited Shemette and Shmerly Gorgis, parents of his late tuba player Shmem. Both are dead, and the whole Gorgis family is gone.
events.detail: Shmem died in the prison riot. His parents were killed as part of the Fury vessel ritual involving Felicia Jr. Sorenson spent the rest of the night at Turckle and Churckle. Neebus is running it incompetently now that Turckle also died in the ritual. The Dragons Claw have the run of the place, and the remaining Fark's Bargain workers now work there too.

events.title: Felicia and Skye Spar
events.summary: The party runs sparring practice with Felicia and Skye. The two try to outdo each other, and a rivalry starts.
events.detail: Felicia had wanted to spar Skye back in Starilaskur, and Lirael had put her off for fear she would kill the girl. Now both train against the party. Baron Hellsauce arrives at the ship to say Morganth wishes to speak with them. The party is not terribly interested.

events.title: Thaddeus Is Coming to Town
events.summary: Posters for Thaddeus's speech paper every wall in Ardev. A House Cannith artificer hands the party a missing-person flyer for Barry.
events.detail: Brand walks the streets painted purple under the hat of slight disguise. The town has been told not to miss the speech. At the forge, the party asks Brokk what happened to Barry. Brokk does not know; Barry disappeared sometime last night.

events.title: Captain Flowers' Black Order
events.summary: Captain Flowers admits the Royal Ardev Regiment's strike on the demon portal outside Hobbstweedle came from a black order. He never learned who sent it.
events.detail: The mission also involved Murphy Gravewood, Kal Valvier and Gauss Hog. Flowers knows he shouldn't tell anyone, but he trusts the party. The story about a training exercise for an attack on Thrane was a cover. Black orders are classified and must be obeyed without question. After the portal was destroyed, the Regiment was disbanded and Flowers was sent back to Ardev to replace the police captain, who had recently died. Soon after, the Dragons Claw mercenaries came to town.

events.title: Morganth on the Sending Stone
events.summary: Through Flowers's sending stone, Morganth asks why Ellis died so brutally and publicly. He then asks the party to cause no incident and not to fly their ship while Thaddeus is in town.
events.detail: Morganth thanks them for speaking with him, and they tell him they did not kill Ellis. He says they have caused several incidents in town, and while they have a job to do, so does he. His direct superior, Art Broadhelm, is coming with Thaddeus to review how the police and the Dragons Claw have been integrated. Flying the airship would be seen as a security risk and would disturb the townsfolk. He knows they care for the town, but protecting it is his job, and he would appreciate them not making it harder today. Annoyed, the party reluctantly agrees. The notes for this session were reconstructed a year later from memory.
